applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content:
SOURCE: Reserve Bank of India
DOCUMENT: Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Commercial Banks (including Regional Rural Banks) and All India Financial Institutions
REFERENCE: RBI/DOS/2024-25/118
DATE: July 15, 2024
JURISDICTION: India
APPLICABILITY: Commercial Banks including RRBs, and All India Financial Institutions

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: These Directions provide a framework to banks for prevention, early detection and timely reporting of incidents of fraud to Law Enforcement Agencies, the Reserve Bank of India and NABARD, along with related fraud risk management requirements.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: Banks shall have a Board-approved Fraud Risk Management Policy defining the roles and responsibilities of the Board, Board Committees and Senior Management.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: Banks shall establish an appropriate organisational structure for fraud risk management within their overall risk management functions. A senior official of at least General Manager rank or equivalent shall be responsible for monitoring and reporting frauds.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: Banks shall maintain a framework for Early Warning Signals (EWS) and Red Flagging of Accounts (RFA) under the Board-approved Fraud Risk Management Policy.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: A Red Flagged Account is an account where one or more Early Warning Signal indicators create suspicion of fraudulent activity and trigger deeper investigation and preventive measures.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: The Risk Management Committee of the Board shall oversee the effectiveness of the EWS and RFA framework, while Senior Management is responsible for implementation.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: Regulated entities are required to maintain robust internal audit and control frameworks as part of fraud risk management.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: Banks shall use appropriate data analytics and market intelligence capabilities to strengthen fraud risk management and support early detection and prevention of fraud.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: The framework includes requirements relating to reporting incidents of fraud to Law Enforcement Agencies and the Reserve Bank of India, as well as maintaining relevant fraud reporting information.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions
content: Fraud classification and related decisions must follow a defined governance process. The Directions require principles of natural justice to be followed in a time-bound manner before persons or entities are classified as fraudulent.

source: RBI - Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2024
applicability: Commercial Banks including RRBs and All India Financial Institutions

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content:
SOURCE: Reserve Bank of India
DOCUMENT: Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
REFERENCE: DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18
DATE: July 6, 2017
JURISDICTION: India
APPLICABILITY: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: The directions establish a framework for limiting customer liability in unauthorised electronic banking transactions and require banks to strengthen systems and procedures for customer protection.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall put in place appropriate systems and procedures to ensure the safety and security of electronic banking transactions carried out by customers.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall maintain robust and dynamic fraud detection and prevention mechanisms.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall assess risks arising from unauthorised transactions, measure liabilities arising from such events, and implement appropriate measures to mitigate those risks.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall require customers to register for SMS alerts and, wherever available, email alerts for electronic banking transactions.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks providing electronic banking services shall provide customers with 24x7 access through multiple channels for reporting unauthorised transactions and loss or theft of payment instruments.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall provide mechanisms allowing customers to report unauthorised transactions through channels such as website, phone banking, SMS, email, IVR and dedicated helplines.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall provide a direct link for reporting unauthorised electronic transactions on their website.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: The reporting system shall provide an immediate acknowledgement of the complaint, including a registered complaint number.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall record the date and time of delivery of transaction alerts and customer responses.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: On receiving a report of an unauthorised transaction, banks shall take immediate steps to prevent further unauthorised transactions in the account.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Customer liability depends on the circumstances of the unauthorised transaction, including whether the incident resulted from bank negligence, customer negligence or a third-party breach.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Where the customer is negligent, such as by sharing payment credentials, the customer bears the loss until the transaction is reported to the bank. Loss occurring after reporting is borne by the bank.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: For certain third-party breaches, customers may have zero liability when they notify the bank within the prescribed time.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: For transactions qualifying for zero or limited liability, the bank shall provide shadow reversal of the amount involved within the prescribed period.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall establish procedures and timelines for resolving complaints and determining customer liability.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall formulate or revise a Board-approved customer relations policy covering customer rights and obligations for unauthorised transactions.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: The policy should include customer awareness, procedures for reporting unauthorised transactions, complaint acknowledgement, grievance redressal, escalation procedures, resolution timelines and compensation.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: The burden of proving customer liability in cases of unauthorised electronic banking transactions shall lie on the bank.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: Banks shall maintain mechanisms for reporting unauthorised electronic banking transaction cases to the Board or an appropriate Board Committee.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
content: The framework also requires monitoring of such transactions and review by internal auditors.

source: RBI - Customer Protection for Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
applicability: Scheduled Commercial Banks including RRBs, Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks
